S57.01.needs: a web search key for Local or BYOK (the menu shows Set up web search when one is needed)
S57.01.note: The menu description says the search runs through the CLI and that Local privacy mode refuses the network.
steps: Click the + button in the chat box and choose Browse the web (it turns on).
Type a question that needs current web information and send it.
Watch the transcript for a web search tool row with its own label and summary.
Click the row to expand it, then look for an "N sources" line under the answer and check the sources are listed.
S57.01.where: AGI Code sidebar > + button (title "Attach or use tools") > Browse the web

labels.text: Read a page by its URL
Code: Choose Tools for This Session

S57.02.needs: a web connection and the Web pages tool ticked
S57.02.note: The chooser requires a CLI capability (turnToolFilters) and shows an error if it is missing.
steps: Run Code: Choose Tools for This Session from the Command Palette.
Make sure Web pages (Read a page by its URL) is ticked and press Enter.
In the chat box, paste a web page address and ask the assistant to read it and summarise it.
Expand the new tool row in the transcript and check its request shows the address and its response shows the page text.
S57.02.where: Command Palette > Code: Choose Tools for This Session > Web pages

S57.03.needs: a PDF or Office file in the open folder
S57.03.note: No separate source-reader control was found; the document reading sits in the CLI documents module and is reached through the file read tool. Whether a cited source is opened by reference was not confirmed in the extension UI.
steps: Open a folder that contains a PDF or Word file.
In the chat box, ask the assistant to read that file and quote a sentence from it.
Expand the file tool row in the transcript.
Check the Snippet section shows text from the document.
S57.03.where: AGI Code sidebar > chat box: ask the assistant to read a PDF or Office file in the workspace

S57.04.needs: a project folder with files containing a known phrase
S57.04.note: Tool row names are built from the tool's internal name at run time, so the exact row title is not a fixed string in the code. The Request or Response label depends on how the tool is classed.
steps: Open a project folder.
In the chat box, ask the assistant to find where a given phrase or file name appears in the project.
Expand the search tool row in the transcript.
Check the request shows the search text and the response lists matching paths or lines.
S57.04.where: AGI Code sidebar > chat box: ask the assistant to find a phrase in the project

S57.05.needs: a text file in the open folder
steps: Open a folder that contains a text file.
In the chat box, ask the assistant to read that file by name and tell you one line from it.
Expand the file tool row in the transcript.
Check the File section shows the path and the Snippet section shows the file text.
S57.05.where: AGI Code sidebar > chat box: ask the assistant to read a named file

S57.06.needs: a folder open in VS Code and an approval if asked
S57.06.note: Whether the write happens in a sandbox or on the machine depends on the session trust mode; not verified.
steps: Open a folder in VS Code.
In the chat box, ask the assistant to create a new file with a given name and one line of text.
Approve the request if the assistant asks for permission.
Expand the file tool row and check the Wrote section shows the file path, and that the file exists in the folder.
S57.06.where: AGI Code sidebar > chat box: ask the assistant to create a new file

S57.10.note: No dedicated code-execution tool was found in the tool catalog (apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/tool_catalog.rs). The nearest is the shell tool (Shell commands), which can run a script the assistant wrote. Searched the extension and CLI for a code-run tool name.

S57.11.needs: a shell available on the machine and the Shell commands tool ticked
steps: Run Code: Choose Tools for This Session and make sure Shell commands is ticked.
In the chat box, ask the assistant to run a harmless command such as node --version.
Expand the command tool row.
Check the Command section shows the command with a $ prefix, and the Output section shows the result with an exit code.
S57.11.where: Command Palette > Code: Choose Tools for This Session > Shell commands, then AGI Code sidebar > chat box

S57.12.needs: an existing file in the open folder
steps: Make sure File edits is ticked in Code: Choose Tools for This Session.
In the chat box, ask the assistant to change one line in an existing file and leave the rest alone.
Expand the edit tool row and click Open diff.
Check the diff changes only the requested line and the row shows a diff summary.
S57.12.where: Command Palette > Code: Choose Tools for This Session > File edits, then AGI Code sidebar > chat box

labels.text: Open, read and act on pages in the paired browser

S57.13.needs: a paired browser; the pairing steps were not found in the extension code
S57.13.note: How a browser gets paired was not found in the extension code.
steps: Make sure Browser is ticked in Code: Choose Tools for This Session.
In the chat box, ask the assistant to open a web address in the browser.
Expand the browser tool row to see the address it used.
Check that a real browser tab opened at that address.
S57.13.where: Command Palette > Code: Choose Tools for This Session > Browser, then AGI Code sidebar > chat box

labels.text: Open, read and act on pages in the paired browser

S57.14.needs: a paired browser with a page open; the pairing steps were not found in the extension code
S57.14.note: The browser action tools are listed in the same Browser group as the navigation tool.
steps: Make sure Browser is ticked in Code: Choose Tools for This Session.
With a page open in the paired browser, ask the assistant to read the page and then click or type in it.
Expand each browser tool row in the transcript.
Check the page in the browser changed as the row describes.
S57.14.where: Command Palette > Code: Choose Tools for This Session > Browser, then AGI Code sidebar > chat box

S57.21.note: The in-turn memory tool has no control of its own; the Code: Memory commands are the user-side view of the same facts.
steps: In the chat box, ask the assistant to remember a fact, such as a preferred test framework.
Approve the save if the assistant asks first.
Run Code: Memory from the Command Palette and check the fact is listed.
In a new chat, ask the assistant what it remembers and check the memory tool row appears with the fact.
S57.21.where: AGI Code sidebar > chat box: ask the assistant to remember a fact; Command Palette > Code: Memory to check it

S57.22.note: No calendar tool was found in the extension or the CLI tool catalog. Calendar appears only as a connector event source for scheduled triggers (apps/cli/src/schedules/triggers.rs) and in the generic connector approval text (apps/cli/src/models/managed_approvals.rs).

S57.23.note: No Slack messaging tool was found. send_message in the CLI catalog is for agent-team teammates, not a connected service. Slack appears only as a schedule trigger source (apps/cli/src/schedules/triggers.rs) and the generic connector approval text.

S57.24.needs: a signed-in AGI account (scheduled work runs in the AGI cloud and cannot be local-only)
S57.24.note: The tool that creates a schedule is cron_create in the CLI catalog. Whether a chat session can call it from this extension was not confirmed.
steps: Run Code: Show Schedules from the Command Palette and note the list.
In the chat box, ask the assistant to schedule a short task every day at nine.
Run Code: Show Schedules again and check the new schedule is listed.
Use Code: Pause Schedule or Code: Run Schedule Now on it and check its state changes.
S57.24.where: Command Palette > Code: Show Schedules; or AGI Code sidebar > chat box: ask the assistant to schedule a task

steps: In the chat box, ask the assistant to hand one sub-task, such as summarising a file, to a subagent and use its answer.
Watch the Subagents panel appear above the transcript and its count change.
Open the subagent transcript if the panel offers it.
Check the main answer uses the subagent result.
S57.25.where: AGI Code sidebar > chat box: ask for a sub-task to be handed to a subagent

steps: In the chat box, ask the assistant to pick a setting for you, and to ask you before it starts.
Check an AGI asks card appears with the question and choice buttons.
Click one choice button.
Check the card closes and the assistant continues with your choice.
S57.26.where: AGI Code sidebar > chat box: ask a request that needs a choice first

S57.28.needs: several tools available to the session
S57.28.note: The effect shows only as a tool search row in the transcript, whose label is built from the tool name. Tool discovery is in apps/cli/src/features/exec/tools/mod.rs.
steps: Connect more tools than fit in one turn, for example by ticking many groups in Code: Choose Tools for This Session.
Ask a task that needs a tool outside the first set.
Check a tool search row appears in the transcript when the assistant loads that tool.
S57.28.where: Inner behaviour: the model is told which other tools exist; no control in the app

labels.text: Code: Choose Tools for This Session

S57.29.note: The typed filter searches only the six tool groups. The model's own tool search (tool_search in apps/cli/src/features/exec/tools/mod.rs) has no control in the app.
steps: Run Code: Choose Tools for This Session from the Command Palette.
Type a word such as browser or web into the list.
Check only the matching tool groups stay in the list and each shows its description.
Press Escape to close without changing anything.
S57.29.where: Command Palette > Code: Choose Tools for This Session, then type a word in the list

S57.31.needs: a folder open in VS Code
steps: In the chat box, ask the assistant to run a shell command such as ls.
Wait for the tool row to appear in the transcript.
Click the tool row to open it.
Check the Command section shows the command with a $ prefix, or the Request section shows the arguments for other tools.
S57.31.where: AGI Code sidebar > chat box: ask for a shell command, then click its tool row

S57.32.needs: a folder open in VS Code
S57.32.note: The code shows a spinner while running, but no live elapsed time; the elapsed time is added only when the tool finishes. Expected says running with elapsed time.
steps: In the chat box, ask the assistant to run a command that waits about 10 seconds, such as sleep 10.
While it runs, check the tool row shows a spinning icon and the activity line counts the action.
When it ends, check the row changes to done, or to an error state.
Check the row summary ends with an elapsed time.
S57.32.where: AGI Code sidebar > chat box: ask for a shell command that takes a few seconds; watch the activity line above the tool rows

S57.33.needs: a folder open in VS Code
S57.33.note: The closed row shows only the label, summary and elapsed time; the result text appears only after the row is opened, so Expected's preview is not visible on the closed row.
steps: In the chat box, ask the assistant to run a short command such as echo hello.
When the row finishes, look at the row without clicking it.
Click the row and check the Output section shows the result text.
Compare the shown text with the command output.
S57.33.where: AGI Code sidebar > chat box: ask for a shell command, then look at the finished tool row

S57.34.needs: a folder open in VS Code
steps: Ask the assistant to run a shell command and wait for its row to finish.
Click the row once and check the Command and Output sections appear.
Click the row again and check it collapses.
Compare what is shown with the request and result.
S57.34.where: AGI Code sidebar > chat box: click any finished tool row

labels.text: full output saved for the user to

S57.36.needs: a folder open in VS Code and an approval if asked
S57.36.note: The reference is plain text with a path; no open button was found in the extension. The path is in the CLI config folder under tool-output.
steps: In the chat box, ask the assistant to run a command with a very long output, such as seq 1 200000.
Approve the command if asked.
Expand the finished tool row and scroll to the end of the Output section.
Check the text says the full output was saved and gives a file path to open.
S57.36.where: AGI Code sidebar > chat box: ask for a command with a very long output, then expand its row

S57.37.needs: a chat session that has run tools
S57.37.note: The receipt lists file changes and approvals, not every tool call with its input and outcome, so Expected is only partly met.
steps: Use an AGI Code chat that ran at least one tool.
Run Code: Show Session Activity from the Command Palette.
Read the list: Details, then Files changed, then Approvals.
Check each file change and approval matches what the tools did in the chat.
S57.37.where: Command Palette > Code: Show Session Activity
